extracted.intended_audience: ORR care provider facilities, PRS providers, grantees/contractors, facility administrators, and other stakeholders responding to the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Federal proposed regulatory standards for Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) care provider facilities, post-release services (PRS) providers, and restrictive settings governing records, behavior management, staff training, language access, healthcare, placement, transfers, and related operational requirements for unaccompanied children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of PRS records in individual case files
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would consider all unaccompanied children's records, including those produced for post-release services (PRS), to be included in the individual case file records of unaccompanied children, whether generated while the child is in ORR custody or after release to their sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRS records are created by or on behalf of ORR and assist ORR in coordinating supportive services for the child and sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and ORR ownership of case file records
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities and PRS providers must maintain the confidentiality of case file records and protect them from unauthorized use or disclosure; records in unaccompanied children's case files are the property of ORR whether in ORR's possession or in the possession of care provider facilities or PRS providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities receiving ORR funding via cooperative agreements must not release case file records or information contained in them for purposes other than program administration without prior ORR approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide case files upon ORR request
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities and PRS providers must provide the case files of unaccompanied children to ORR immediately upon ORR's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures ORR can consider whether disclosure meets program goals and safeguards child/sponsor privacy and protected health information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on disclosure by employees/contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees, former employees, or contractors of a care provider facility or PRS provider must not disclose case file records or provide information about unaccompanied children, their sponsors, family or household members to anyone except for program administration without first providing advance notice to ORR of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice allows ORR to ensure disclosures are compatible with program goals, protect safety/privacy, and comply with statutes and federal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-approved limited disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR policy is to pre-approve certain limited disclosures by ORR grantees and contractors for specific routine or emergency purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-approved disclosures include (1) registration for school and other routine educational purposes; (2) routine medical, dental, or mental health treatment; (3) emergency medical care; (4) to obtain services in accordance with ORR policies; and (5) pursuant to whistleblower protection laws — allowing expeditious provision of routine/emergency services without prior ORR approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records maintenance and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs must maintain adequate records and make regular reports as required by ORR to permit ORR to monitor and enforce regulations and other requirements and standards ORR determines are in the best interests of each unaccompanied child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR welcomes public comment on these proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior management strategies: evidence-based and trauma-informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must develop behavior management strategies that include evidence-based, trauma-informed, and linguistically responsive program rules and behavior management policies that consider the range of ages and maturity and are culturally sensitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include setting clear expectations, creating structured routines, using positive reinforcement, avoiding negative reinforcement, fostering cooperation, problem-solving, healthy de-escalation, and positive behavioral management skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on negative reinforcement and non-constructive consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavior management strategies must not use practices that involve negative reinforcement or consequences/measures that are not constructive or not logically related to the behavior being regulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically prohibits corporal punishment, use of significant incident reports as punishment, unfavorable consequences related to family/sponsor unification or legal matters (e.g., immigration/asylum), forced chores/activities intended to demean or humiliate, forced physical movement (e.g., push-ups, running), uncomfortable physical positions as punishment, searches of personal belongings solely for behavior management, and medical interventions not prescribed by a medical provider acting within usual professional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions limitations (health, basic needs, services)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any sanctions employed must not adversely affect an unaccompanied child's health or physical, emotional, or psychological well-being, nor deny meals, hydration, sufficient sleep, routine personal grooming activities, exercise (including daily outdoor activity), medical care, correspondence or communication privileges, or legal assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to protect fundamental needs and access to mandated services while addressing behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute prohibition on prone, chemical, and peer restraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of prone physical restraints, chemical restraints, or peer restraints is prohibited for any reason in any care provider facility setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies across facility types under proposed § 410.1304(a)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: De-escalation and staff training requirements for behavior management
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff must be trained on the facility's behavior management strategies, including de-escalation techniques; involvement of law enforcement is a last resort and calls may trigger staff evaluation regarding qualifications and training in trauma-informed, de-escalation techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed § 410.1305 requires training topics (see separate metric) and that trainings be tailored to the unique needs, attributes, and gender of children at the facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training topics and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Training should include the rights of unaccompanied children, creating bias-free environments, supporting children with disabilities, supporting mental health needs, trauma, child development, prevention of sexual abuse, identification of victims of human trafficking, racial and cultural sensitivity, and training on behavior management/de-escalation; case managers should be trained on child welfare best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care provider facilities must document completion of all trainings in personnel files; staff, contractors, and volunteers must receive training and understand obligations under ORR regulations and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background checks and vetting
rubrics_metrics.description: All staff must complete background check requirements and vetting for their respective roles prior to service provision, and care provider facilities must provide documentation to ORR of compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to staff, contractors, and volunteers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law enforcement as last resort and required pre-engagement process (request for comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls to law enforcement are not to be considered a behavior management strategy; facilities are expected to apply other means to de-escalate, and ORR requests comment on what process should be required before engaging law enforcement (e.g., de-escalation strategies that must first be attempted and specific behaviors that warrant law enforcement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In emergencies or safety-of-child-or-staff situations, 9-1-1 may be called; such calls may trigger staff qualification/training evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on seclusion as behavioral intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs and RTCs are prohibited from using seclusion as a behavioral intervention (this does not apply to medically necessary isolation/quarantine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restraints are also prohibited except as expressly described for emergencies; personal restraint permitted only in emergency safety situations after de-escalation attempts have failed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted emergency restraints in secure facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure facilities (not including RTCs) may use personal restraints, mechanical restraints, and/or seclusion in emergency safety situations, subject to other prohibitions (e.g., no prone/chemical/peer restraints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such measures are only for emergency safety situations and ORR emphasizes prevention and use only after less restrictive measures fail; all care provider facilities must report emergency/major incidents to ORR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint rules for transport and court/asylum interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure facilities may restrain a child for their immediate safety or that of others during transport to immigration court or asylum interview and may restrain in court/interview if the child exhibits imminent runaway behavior, makes violent threats, demonstrates violent behavior, or an individualized determination finds serious risk of violence or running away; immigration judges retain discretion to provide input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities must provide all mandated services to the greatest extent practicable while ensuring safety when restraints are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of soft restraints during transport
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities may use soft restraints (e.g., zip ties, leg or ankle weights) only during transport to and from secure facilities, and only when the care provider believes a child poses a serious risk of physical harm to self/others or a serious risk of running away from ORR custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitations are meant to narrowly permit only transport-related uses where risk is high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff-to-child ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs and restrictive placements must meet staff-to-child ratios established by their states or other licensing entities, or ratios established by ORR if state licensure is not available; ORR generally requires a minimum of 1 staff to 8 children during the day and 1 staff to 16 children at night while children sleep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If state requirements are stricter, the facility must abide by the smaller (stricter) ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case management staffing and placement of case managers
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs and restrictive placements are required to provide case management services, have case managers based at the facility site, and ensure case manager-to-child ratios take occupancy into account and are appropriate to meet ORR's standards for length of care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR may determine appropriate ratios via cooperative agreements and contracts to allow adjustments relative to occupancy and policies related to length of stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent offering of interpretation and translation services to children
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must, to the greatest extent practicable, consistently offer all unaccompanied children the option of interpretation and translation services in their native or preferred language and in a way they understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes furnishing auxiliary aids/services (qualified sign language interpreters, Braille, audio, note-takers) per 45 CFR 85.51; facilities must translate all documents/materials shared with children in a timely manner; professional telephonic interpretation permitted only after reasonable efforts to obtain in-person qualified interpreters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement informed by language access considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Placement decisions should be informed by language access considerations; ORR would, to the extent appropriate and practicable, place children with similar language needs within the same standard program or restrictive placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aims to ensure efficient use of resources and timely, appropriate placement while considering individualized needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language access during intake, orientation, and confidentiality notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must provide a written notice of limits of confidentiality and orally explain it in the child's native/preferred language prior to completion of the UC Assessment and prior to starting counseling; assessments and initial medical exams must be conducted in the child's native/preferred language; standardized orientation must be provided within 48 hours of admission in a way the child effectively understands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For step-ups/step-downs, facilities must explain placement changes in the child's native/preferred language; if the child is not literate, a qualified interpreter must orally/sign-translate all documents and confirm comprehension; facilities must document in the case file that the child acknowledged understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language access in education
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard programs and heightened supervision facilities must provide educational instruction and relevant materials in formats and languages accessible to all children (in-person interpretation, telephonic interpretation, written translations by qualified interpreters), provide recreational reading materials in accessible formats/languages, and translate ORR-required documents used in educational lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures promote meaningful education services regardless of native language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodation of religious and cultural expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities should accommodate children's religious and cultural expressions, practices, and identities to the extent practicable; when a child makes a reasonable request for religious/cultural items (e.g., books, clothing), the facility must provide applicable items in the child's native/preferred language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR operates in compliance with the Religious Freedom Restoration Act and other federal conscience and civil rights protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language access for parents/guardians/potential sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must utilize necessary professional interpretation/translation services to ensure meaningful access by parents, guardians, and potential sponsors, and translate all documents and materials shared with them in their native/preferred language; facilities must ensure effective communication with parents/guardians/potential sponsors with disabilities per 45 CFR 85.51.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures family/sponsor understanding and participation in post-release processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language access during healthcare encounters
rubrics_metrics.description: While children are receiving healthcare services, facilities must ensure children can communicate with physicians, clinicians, and healthcare staff in their native/preferred language and in a way they effectively understand, prioritizing in-person qualified interpreters before telephonic services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritization reflects importance of accurate in-person interpretation in medical contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language access for legal services and interpreter confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must make qualified interpretation/translation services available upon request to children, child advocates, and legal service providers when children receive legal services; interpreters and translators must keep information about children's cases/services confidential from non-ORR grantees, contractors, and Federal staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This promotes effective legal representation and preserves confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of appropriate healthcare services
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall ensure provision of appropriate routine medical and dental care; access to medical services requiring heightened ORR involvement; family planning services; and emergency health services in standard programs and restrictive placements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifies corresponding requirements from Exhibit 1 of the FSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network of licensed healthcare providers and initial exams
rubrics_metrics.description: Care providers must establish a network of licensed healthcare providers (including specialists, emergency care, mental health, dental) that accept ORR's fee-for-service billing; unaccompanied children must receive a complete medical examination (including infectious disease screening) within two business days of admission unless recently examined elsewhere; if still in ORR custody 60–90 days after admission, an initial dental exam is required (or sooner if state rules direct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures timely baseline medical/dental assessment and access to necessary specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required immunizations and annual exams
rubrics_metrics.description: Care providers must require appropriate immunizations as recommended by the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule and approved by CDC; providers must require an annual physical exam including hearing and vision screening and follow-up care for acute and chronic conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aids early detection and management of health conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration of medications, special diets, and mental health interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would require administration of prescribed medication and special diets and appropriate mental health interventions when necessary, including routine individual and group counseling sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care provider facilities must facilitate ordered/scheduled treatments as prescribed by licensed healthcare providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies for communicable disease control
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must have policies/procedures for identifying, reporting, and controlling communicable diseases consistent with applicable State, local, and Federal laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These policies support prevention of disease spread and protect facility populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of healthcare requests (language/literacy barriers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must have policies/procedures enabling unaccompanied children, including those with language and literacy barriers, to convey written and oral requests for emergency and non-emergency healthcare services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures children can request and access care regardless of language or literacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medication safety, storage, administration, and authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must have policies/procedures based on state/local laws to ensure safe, discreet, and confidential provision of prescription and nonprescription medications, secure storage, and controlled administration and disposal of all drugs; a licensed healthcare provider must write or orally order all nonprescription medications and oral orders must be documented in the child's file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to prevent medication errors, diversion, and breaches of confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical isolation/quarantine limited and accompanied by services
rubrics_metrics.description: Placement in medical isolation/exclusion from general population is permitted when medically necessary to prevent spread of infectious disease or as required by law, but must be limited to only the extent necessary to ensure health/welfare; isolated children must still be provided mandated services to the greatest extent practicable and be supervised under applicable ratios; multiple isolated children should be placed together when practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes medically required isolation from prohibited seclusion as behavioral intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement decisions informed by medical needs and transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes that to the greatest extent possible, children requiring medical care or who reasonably request medical care be placed in facilities with appropriate bed space and access to relevant medical services; if initial placement is not available or needs arise after the Initial Medical Exam, ORR shall transfer the child to an accommodating facility and care provider must notify ORR immediately and submit a transfer recommendation within three business days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns placement with the least restrictive, best-interest standard and subpart G transfer procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation for medical and ancillary services
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes requirements ensuring children are provided transportation to access medical services (including across state lines if necessary) and associated ancillary services so they can access specialists, family planning, prenatal care, or geographically limited care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with current policy that ORR or its care provider facilities provide transportation for service provision including medical services.
